body: Held for round 2 — **serial, not blocked**. This card imports the shared origin constant that #12232 (dispatched now) owns creating; dispatching both at once means two agents creating the same file. Known trap to carry into the dispatch: read what #12232 actually exported before writing the import, and do not re-create the constant if it is already on `main` by then. #12235 is queued behind this card because it edits the same `generateMetadata` block.

⚠️ Trap carried in from #12232's dev report — read before starting this card.

`apps/docs/app/page.tsx` is a **shadowed route**: `proxy.ts` rewrites `/` to `/en`, so `RootPage()` never runs (measured: `curl /` returns `200 text/html`, not the 307 that file would produce). Filed standalone as #12255.

What it means here: the homepage's real metadata lives in `apps/docs/app/[lang]/page.tsx`. An agent that adds `metadataBase` or a canonical link to `app/page.tsx` will ship a green PR that changes nothing served. Verify against a rendered response, not against the file you edited.

The epic does not depend on #12255 being fixed — it stays a standalone finding — but this card does depend on knowing about it.

$ grep -rn "metadataBase\|canonical\|alternates" apps/docs --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'
apps/docs/lib/site.ts:6,11,12,26   <- prose in the docblock only, no usage
$ grep -rn "generateMetadata\|export const metadata" apps/docs --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'
apps/docs/app/layout.tsx:5

apps/docs/app/[lang]/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx:56
apps/docs/app/[lang]/blog/[[...slug]]/page.tsx:183

Positive control returns 4 hits, so the zero is absence, not a broken query. Premise holds.

`apps/docs/lib/site.ts` is on `main` and will be imported, not re-created. `apps/docs/app/page.tsx` (shadowed, #12255) will not be touched; every claim gets verified against a rendered response.

**ACCEPT** — PR #12305, 4 files, **+32/-0**, pure additions on exactly the declared surface, importing the existing `lib/site.ts` rather than re-creating it.

- **Correction to my assumption 3, and it is the useful kind**: the route tree has **five** URL shapes, not the four I listed. I omitted `/docs` — the empty-slug case of the docs optional catch-all, which resolves `content/docs/index.mdx`. All five now emit exactly one absolute canonical, verified against a `next build && next start` server rather than against the edited files.
- **Query-string case measured**: `/docs/data-modeling/objects?utm_source=y&gclid=z` canonicalises to the clean URL, byte-identical to what the clean URL emits.
- **An acceptance box reported as vacuous instead of ticked**: "the build stops warning about a missing `metadataBase`" — the base build never warned, because Next only warns when metadata holds a *relative* URL needing resolution, and there were none. Rather than claim a fix for a warning that never fired, the dev ran a second ablation (remove `metadataBase`, add a relative `openGraph.images`) and made the warning appear, proving it is live and that the box is satisfied vacuously rather than untested. That distinction is the whole difference between a verified gate and a green light nobody checked.
- **Absolute canonicals via `absoluteUrl()` rather than `metadataBase`-relative ones**, deliberately: the helper throws at build time on a non-site-relative path, and it is the same helper `app/sitemap.ts` uses, so the canonical link and the sitemap entry read one constant and cannot drift.
- **Flagged, not a defect, and I agree with the reading**: the homepage canonical renders `https://objectstack.ai` while the sitemap emits `https://objectstack.ai/`. RFC 3986 §6.2.3 makes an empty path equivalent to `/` and search engines normalise them identically. Harmonising would mean editing `app/sitemap.ts`, outside the declared surface — correctly flagged instead of reached for. No follow-up card: a card for a non-defect is noise.

⚠️ For **#12235** (Open Graph), which is queued behind this: `metadataBase` is now set, so relative image URLs resolve. That was the dependency this card existed to satisfy.
